title: Seeds, noise and determinism
hook: A seed makes the starting noise, plus the extra noise of an ancestral sampler, and nothing more. A toy sampler with an exact denoiser shows what that does and does not fix when you change steps, samplers or hardware.

verified.claim: prepare_noise seeds PyTorch's generator and draws on the CPU in float32.
default_noise_sampler seeds a generator on the latent's device, adding 1 on the CPU.
noise_scaling multiplies by the square root of 1 + sigma squared at full denoise, and adds the latent in both branches.
The seed widget's range is 0 to 0xffffffffffffffff with control_after_generate.
The noise, the sum and the toy samplers come from running the lab on the CPU.
The three pictures come from the same seed (424242), the same prompt and 20 steps, per the Sampling Lab's renders.json. We looked at all three.
The browser lab's step rules follow sample_euler and get_ancestral_step, in one dimension, with our own generator.

unchecked: The pictures are one seed on one model. They show what can happen, and no rate.
We did not compare the same seed across two machines. The warning there comes from PyTorch's notes.
